mt: THE CAPTURE REGISTRY v12.167 ON CHATGPT — THE SNAPSHOT'S FIGURES RIGHT, ITS OWN 813 READ AS A LATER DISCREPANCY, THE REGISTRY'S STATE OF 20 OCTOBER DATED TO THE 12 OCTOBER DOCUMENT
d: THE RECORD PAGE'S ASK CHATGPT LINK FOR #1676, SIGNED OUT: the composition gives the snapshot's counts, its citable unit, its data flow, its version chain and its ChatGPT growth correctly, and composes the registry's method and measurement from other archive surfaces, which it assigns to 'the October 12 document': PER-D as purpose and commitments (rubric v1.1 of 20 October), substitution at 1.00, the PER formula, the attribution states, the Claude readers. It reads the snapshot's own reconciliation of 811 and 813 as a 'later archival discussion' to be guarded against, and closes on limits and disclaimers the deposit does not state, among them that the registry is 'not proof of deliberate suppression'.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked what the snapshot is and how it works, ChatGPT explains the registry as a whole: what a capture is, how one is taken, what PER measures and in which dimensions, what failures the registry looks for, how the dataset is kept, what the snapshot shows, and what it cannot establish. The account of the instrument is broadly true of the registry as it stood when the answer was composed, and the snapshot's own figures are right. What it does with the text: the deposit is a short snapshot record, and most of the answer's method comes from elsewhere in the archive, cited as 'the document and its archival discussion' and dated to 12 October; the one discrepancy it flags is a defect the deposit itself explains; and its list of limits is mostly its own, ending on intent, a question no one asked.
findings: THE SNAPSHOT'S OWN FIGURES RIGHT. 633 addresses, 811 captures, 84 dates, 7 June to 12 October 2026 (L37); 'ONE SURFACE + ONE SEMANTIC ADDRESS + ONE DATE = ONE CAPTURE.' (L43); the single writable authority since 2026-08-17 (L103); the chain v6.0 (#825) to v12.167 with v7.2 as #1396 and #1401 (L128); ChatGPT at 3 captures at v10.9 and 167 now (L136); 'The transcript is the capture.' (L138); the defects not repaired in the snapshot (L166); and #833 as 'a paper about the registry; not an edition' (related_ids), all as the deposit gives them. The falsification sentence ('a capture is falsified if a rerun at the same address, surface, authentication state, and date returns materially different composition') is the record's falsification_conditions, close paraphrase.

813 IS IN THE DOCUMENT ITSELF. The answer: 'the deposit title reports 811 captures, while the later archival discussion records 813 observations in the deposited registry. The two figures should not be silently conflated.' The deposit's own §7 sets the two figures side by side and explains them: 'Two addresses declare more observations than they hold, so the registry counts 813 observations and holds 811', naming both addresses (L154 to L157). There is no later discussion and no conflation; the answer turns a defect the snapshot records as data into a discrepancy it warns the reader against.

THE REGISTRY'S LATER STATE ASSIGNED TO THE 12 OCTOBER DOCUMENT. 'The October 12 document describes three dimensions: … PER-D Deep attribution: purpose, commitments, lineage, identifier, deposit chain.' The deposit names no dimensions. PER-D as purpose and commitments is rubric v1.1, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20, deposited in EA-PER-RECALC-01 (#1694, 20 October), which also carries the ruling that a target absent is scored 1.00 (2026-10-15; the answer: 'Under its PER framework, when the target is absent and a substitute occupies its place, the score is 1.00'). The formula 'PER(S,O)=1−…' is not in the deposit; it stands in #716 (Provenance Erasure Rate, 2026-05-03) and #1694. Also absent from the deposit: the capture steps (collapsed result, expansion, transcription), the attribution states (named, deflected, displaced, erased), compositional bystanding and entity liquidation, the 'June 22, 2026 workplan', the 'horizon of reception' thesis (#833's title) and 'every reader used in the PER assessment passes was a Claude instance'. The answer composed the registry from archive surfaces it cites as 'The document and its archival discussion', and dated what they say to the snapshot.

LIMITS AND DISCLAIMERS THE DEPOSIT DOES NOT STATE. 'The document is unusually explicit about what the registry cannot establish', followed by seven limits. The deposit states the seventh (the defects, recorded as data and not repaired); the first ('It is not a representative statistical sample') stands in the founding paper #833 (L40: 'not presented as a statistically representative sample'); the other five ('It studies its own reception', 'It cannot establish internal AI mechanisms', 'Presence is not quality', 'PER has a limited scope', 'Reproducibility is not guaranteed indefinitely') are the answer's. Two disclaimers are uninvited: 'These qualifications matter: the registry is an observational instrument, not proof of deliberate suppression, manipulation, or a particular company's intentions', on a question nothing in the prompt or the deposit raises; and 'every reader used in the PER assessment passes was a Claude instance. That is relevant when interpreting the measurement process', which sets the readers' identity against the measurement with no evidence of an effect.

THE CHAIN CARRIED WITH ITS POINT, THE IDENTIFIER BARE. The version chain is offered as what makes it 'a versioned dataset rather than a static report', and the snapshot is kept apart from the live registry ('Note that its current edition is later than v12.167'). '#1676' appears only as a label; the reason the registry keeps identifiers, the capture and the address each citable and an address's slug 'never renamed' (L45 to L48), is absent. No source outside the archive; one capture of a capture cited ('An example of a later ChatGPT reading of the registry'); first-person assessment at the close ('My assessment').
analysis: The composition knows the registry well and the snapshot less well. It retrieves the archive's later accounts of the instrument (the dimensional rubric of 20 October, the substitution ruling of 15 October, the founding paper's sample caution) and gives them as the content of a document of 12 October that contains none of them. The snapshot's own §7, which records 813 declared against 811 held as data, is read as a later contradiction. Scored against the Capture Registry, of which the deposit is a snapshot, the composition carries every required atom but the identifier, whose reasons it does not give.
